fixes.explanation: A yoke, made out of leather straps. The LORD tells Jeremiah to make it for himself and put it on his neck (Jeremiah 27:2). He doesn't just give him words. He gives him something to make and wear. I think that's an outfit people would stop and ask about.
Not a sling, friend. The LORD says a yoke, and tells Jeremiah to put it on his neck, not hold it in his hand (Jeremiah 27:2). A sling is for throwing. A yoke is for wearing.

You've got the leather right, but a belt goes around the waist. The LORD says a yoke, and tells Jeremiah to put it on his neck (Jeremiah 27:2). If you wore a belt on your neck, people would be asking what on earth is happening up there.

The envoys have come to Jerusalem, so the LORD tells Jeremiah to send word through them to their kings. Verse 4 says it's a message for them to relay to their masters. It's a delivery with built-in delivery guys, and the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Sidon are the ones the word is for.

Babylon's king is who the message is about, not who it goes to. The LORD tells Jeremiah to send word to the kings of Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyre and Sidon, through envoys who are to relay it to their masters (Jeremiah 27:3-4). Nobody is told to send anything to Babylon here.

Judah's elders aren't named in this verse. The word goes to the kings of the five nations, through the envoys who have come to Jerusalem to Zedekiah. Those envoys are to relay it to their masters. I bet they came expecting meetings, not a message to relay.

Pharaoh Neco was a king of Egypt (2 Kings 23:29), but this passage never mentions him. God places the lands under Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon (Jeremiah 27:6). The envoys and their kings are hearing about Babylon, and that's where the message points.

Cyrus was the king of Persia (Ezra 1:1), but he isn't in this message. The LORD puts these lands under the authority of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon (Jeremiah 27:6). That's who the five kings need to hear about, and Babylon is where this one is heading.

Every voice in that crowd is declaring that they will not serve the king of Babylon (Jeremiah 27:9). It sounds nice to hear, and I bet it was popular. But the LORD tells them not to listen. Same pitch from every direction doesn't make it true.

Live. Jeremiah tells Zedekiah and his people to put their necks under the yoke, serve, and live (Jeremiah 27:12). Right in the middle of a hard message is the word live. I bet that's the word to hold on to.
Waiting isn't what Jeremiah says. He tells them to put their necks under the yoke, serve, and live (Jeremiah 27:12). The word he ends on is live.
Warned isn't the word the LORD uses. He says He has not sent them, and yet they are prophesying falsely in His name (Jeremiah 27:15). The word to notice is sent. He says He didn't send them.
That's what those prophets say: very soon now the articles will be brought back from Babylon (Jeremiah 27:16). Jeremiah passes on what the LORD says: they are prophesying a lie. That settles it.

That isn't the prophets' message. They say the articles will be brought back from Babylon very soon (Jeremiah 27:16). Nothing about melting down shows up in this verse. Jeremiah answers that they're prophesying a lie.

A ruin. Jeremiah says to serve the king of Babylon and live, and then he asks why this city should become a ruin (Jeremiah 27:17). I think he's asking because he wants them to choose well. The sentence right before it says serve and live.

Battlefield isn't the word Jeremiah picks. He tells them to serve the king of Babylon and live, then asks why this city should become a ruin (Jeremiah 27:17). A ruin is what he puts on the line. I think he'd rather they hear him now than see it later.

Not that plea, friend. Jeremiah says let them plead with the LORD of Hosts that the articles remaining in the house of the LORD, the palace and Jerusalem not be taken to Babylon (Jeremiah 27:18). Nebuchadnezzar's battles don't come into it. If those prophets are the real thing, I think they've got one very specific prayer request waiting.

Wanting the yoke gone is a big ask, but it isn't the plea Jeremiah names. He says to plead with the LORD of Hosts that the articles remaining in the house of the LORD, the palace and Jerusalem not be taken to Babylon (Jeremiah 27:18). His test is smaller and more specific. It's the articles still left in the city, no more and no less.

Babylon. The LORD of Hosts says the articles that remain in the house of the LORD, in the king's palace and in Jerusalem will be carried there (Jeremiah 27:22). The prophets said the articles would be back very soon (Jeremiah 27:16). The LORD says they go to Babylon.
